verifiers.claim: stat and read return the revision the content came from on every provider; two providers never issue the same identity for different files.
Two writers over four revisions: no commit succeeds on a stale observed revision, whatever the interleaving.
A stale expectedRevision returns a conflict naming the current revision and leaves content and receipts untouched, on memory, directory and GitHub providers.
create on an existing address and update on a missing one both fail without side effects, on every provider.
remove needs the current revision; a recreate with the same content yields a later revision; the removed revision is never current again.

Traversal, absolute, encoded, aliased and symlinked paths are refused before any provider call, with the one canonical spelling used for storage; the router confines an address to a mount in the table; a run's tool argument cannot reach a mount its grants do not cover.
A write made by the agent's tool is read at the same revision by the host through the same provider, and its receipt matches.

On the registry host over HTTP: the agent's write_file, the page's file routes and the tree read the same revision; the page's save through the routes is what the agent's provider serves next; /code refuses writes on every path.

Every accepted write or removal records one receipt with actor, thread, run, tool and both revisions inside the provider's critical section; a refused or failed one records nothing; concurrent writers at one observed revision yield one receipt.

The GitHub provider lets the far side decide conflicts, reports unverified instead of success when the answer carries no commit or the network fails, keeps no credential, and refuses writes on a pinned ref; the readonly wrapper refuses every mutation.
